name: Warmington Mill

layers.essential_history: [[c:Warmington Mill is mentioned in the Domesday Book. The building you see now is newer, and milling here stopped in 1958.]]
layers.deeper_history: [[c:A mill at Warmington is recorded in 1086 (Domesday) and again in 1125. The building you see now dates from the early or mid 19th century, with a rebuild recorded in 1838, and in 1847 and 1862 it was advertised for sale as a working corn mill with four pairs of stones. It's Grade II listed. The village board says the mill closed in 1958 when Matthew Hayes retired.]]
layers.mystery: [[c:Journal page: you check the mill's records against the estate's own.]]

puzzle.title: The missing sacks
puzzle.intro: [[c:Compare the mill's record with the estate's.]]
material: [[c:MILL RECORD: 12 sacks of grain sent to the estate.]]
[[c:RIVERSIDE NOTE: marked with the same sack symbol, it shows two sacks sold to a private buyer.]]
puzzle.question: [[c:How many sacks are missing?]]
hints: [[c:Compare the number sent with the number received.]]
[[c:Take the smaller number from the larger.]]
puzzle.reveal: [[c:Two sacks are missing, and the riverside note shows where they went. The grain accounts don't add up.]]
puzzle.fallback: [[c:You can work this one out from the clues above.]]

evidence: [[c:The mill sent 12 sacks but the estate only received 10. Two went to a private buyer, so the grain accounts don't add up.]]
